question.text: During a New Fund Offer (NFO) for an open-ended scheme, what is the typical sequence of events?

answer.text: Re-opening for sale/repurchase → Subscription → Allotment → Launch
Subscription → Launch → Re-opening for sale/repurchase → Allotment
Launch → Subscription → Allotment → Re-opening for ongoing sale/repurchase
Allotment → Launch → Subscription → Re-opening for sale/repurchase

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series V-A (p.164-p.165, p.170, p.218), the NFO process for an open-ended scheme follows this sequence: (1) Launch — the AMC publicises the NFO and files documents; (2) Subscription — the NFO opens and closes during a specified period; (3) Allotment — units are allotted (and refunds processed where applicable) within 5 business days of the NFO close; (4) Re-opening for ongoing sale and repurchase — within 5 business days of allotment, the open-ended scheme re-opens for continuous transactions. The Trap: Option B puts launch after subscription, which is sequentially impossible. Option D puts allotment before launch. The source distinguishes between close-ended schemes (which are listed on a stock exchange after allotment) and open-ended schemes (which re-open for sale/repurchase) — for open-ended schemes the correct final step is re-opening, not listing. Note: The 5-business-day turnaround time for both allotment and re-opening is specified in the workbook's regulatory turnaround-time guidance (p.218).
